newsitem.title: USA: Brazil 97-98 coffee crop seen at 23.5 mln - Tristao.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 97-98 coffee crop seen at 23.5 mln - Tristao.

text.p: Brazilian exporter Tristao Group has estimated the country's coffee production will fall to 23.5 million 60-kg bags in the 1997-98 crop year from some 27.5 million bags in the previous harvest.

The Tristao forecast exceeds last month's Brazilian government estimate of 20 million to 22 million bags for the 1997-98 harvest, but it falls well short of private coffee consultant Leon Yallouz's reported forecast of 27.5 million bags.
"While all new trees and those that were pruned after the frost of 1994 have good amounts of cherries, the plantations older than nine years are in general very sparce," the Tristao report said.

"The reasons for this irregular picture are many, but the agronomists and producers have not reached a consensus. We would say that regionally this can be attributed to the occurence of many flowerings rather than one main flowering as normal," it said.
"The reduction of the conilon crop is attributed to the drought in September and October in Espirito Santo," it added.

Still, rainfall in the last months has been "extremely favorable to the maturity and cherries, which allied to the attractive prices, can result in an early harvesting," the report said. "As to the trees, in general they are in excellent condition, showing strong production potential for the 1998-99 crop."
((-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk))
